It generally works best to cook the bacon separately first, and then either add the cabbage when the bacon is almost done (if you're doing cabbage--shredded cabbage cooks pretty fast) or use the fat to roast the sprouts in and then crumble or chop the cooked bacon and add it to the sprouts for the last five-ten minutes of roasting (if you're doing that, make sure the bacon is just cooked when you add it, or it might burn). If you want it to be a full meal instead of a side dish, use more bacon; for a side dish I might only have two or three slices of bacon in there, but for a full meal I want two or three slices per person, roughly--it depends on how many sprouts I have and how much everyone bacon everyone wants. Sometimes I put it over rice or serve it with steamed/boiled potatoes with a little butter, to round out the meal a little more.

I sometimes add a splash of white wine to the cabbage's very hot pan, too, after it's well-coated in the oil and pretty close to done, then give it a stir, cover the pan, and let it sit just a couple of minutes. (Cover the pan after the alcohol has burned off, so the cabbage doesn't have that raw-wine taste.) That's, like, the "dressier" way to do it, though, and it's just as good if not sometimes better without it. Oh, and if I'm doing that I also add a little garlic, which is actually good with either way of doing it (and with the bacon & sprouts, too).
